data.name: Armaan
data.gender_notes: Armaan is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Armaan is a graceful and poetic name of Arabic origin, meaning 'wish', 'desire', or 'hope'. It reflects an emotional and dreamy personality filled with aspirations and inner longing for beauty and goodness. The name Armaan carries the meaning “Wish, Desire, Hope” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Armaan usually hope their child will grow to embody wish, desire, hope and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents a soul filled with noble dreams and heartfelt prayers — someone whose desires are aligned with good intentions.
data.etymology: Armaan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wish, Desire, Hope.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Armaan total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: أرمان
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أرمان مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ر-م-ن' والذي يعني الرغبة أو التمني. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في عدة مواضع، منها قول الله تعالى: 'وَرَمَضَنا بِأَسماعِنا فَلا يَسلَمُ مِنها سَمعٌ' (الفرقان: 22). ويرتبط هذا الاسم بالآمال والرغبات الطيبة في الإسلام.

in_urdu.name: ارمان
in_urdu.long_meaning: ارمان کا نام عربی جڑ 'ر-م-ن' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے خواہش یا آرزو۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں خاصی اہمیت رکھتا ہے۔ اس کا ذکر اسلامی عقیدے میں امید اور تمنا کے طور پر کیا گیا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अरमान
in_hindi.long_meaning: अरमान नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी मूल 'र-म-न' से हुई है जिसका अर्थ है इच्छा या आकांक्षा। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में विशेष महत्व रखता है और इसे उम्मीद और तमन्ना के प्रतीक के रूप में देखा जाता है।

in_pashto.name: ارمان
in_pashto.long_meaning: د ارمان نوم عربي ريښې 'ر-م-ن' څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې معنی یې غواښه یا هیله ده. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو په دودیزو ارزښو کې ځانګړی اهمیت لري او د ښو هیوادونو او تمنو سره تړاو لري.

in_english.name: Armaan
in_english.long_meaning: The name Armaan originates from the Arabic root 'ر-م-ن' (R-M-N), meaning desire, wish, or hope. It appears in various contexts within Islamic tradition, symbolizing good intentions and aspirations. The name carries spiritual significance, representing the optimistic outlook and positive ambitions valued in Muslim cultures.

data.cultural_impact: Armaan is a name deeply rooted in Arab and Islamic culture. In the Islamic tradition, it is a reminder of the deep importance of dhikr, or remembrance of Allah, and seeking His Pleasure in all aspects of life. The name Armaan is a reflection of the human desire to constantly nurture one's relationship with the Divine.
data.spiritual_significance: Armaan holds a significant spiritual meaning in the Islamic tradition. It serves as a reminder of the fundamental concept of tawakkul, or trust and reliance upon Allah. It emphasizes the importance of surrendering oneself to the Will of God and seeking His Guidance to fulfill one's deepest desires and aspirations. Hence, this name carries an essence of deep spiritual meaning, inspiring the bearer to constantly strive towards self-improvement, inner peace, and a closer connection to the Creator.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Armaan: Wish or Desire granted by Allah. The name signifies one who is entrusted with Allah's immense blessings and gifts. It's a reminder to use these blessings wisely and thankfully.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Armaan was a Persian nobleman during the Sassanid Empire. The name Armaan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Armaan was a prominent figure in Persian society during the Sassanid Empire.

modern_usage.modern_context: Armaan is a name of Persian origin that is popular in various parts of the world, particularly in countries with large Muslim populations. It is often given to boys and is associated with nobility, generosity, and kindness.
